If I witness a child being born 5 light years away and then travel to him at the speed of light, how old would the child be from his perspective when I arrive? Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.assistant

Let's break down the problem step by step.

    From your perspective, you witness the birth of the child 5 light years away. This means that the child is born at a distance of 5 light years from you, and you see the light from the birth signal traveling towards you at the speed of light.

    As you travel towards the child at the speed of light, time dilation occurs due to special relativity. From your perspective, time appears to slow down for you relative to the child.

    Since you are traveling at the speed of light, you will experience time dilation to the maximum extent possible. From your perspective, time will appear to stand still for you, while the child will experience time passing normally.

    When you arrive at the child's location, you will have traveled for 5 years from your perspective (since you were traveling at the speed of light). However, from the child's perspective, time has passed normally, and the child will be 5 years old.

    So, from the child's perspective, you will arrive when the child is 5 years old.

    Note that this is a thought experiment, and it's not possible to travel at the speed of light in reality. However, it's an interesting way to explore the concept of time dilation and its effects on relative motion.
